children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose more than 1% on Monday, led by gains in chipmakers after upbeat domestic export data and a rally in US semiconductor stocks in the previous session.
** The benchmark KOSPI
ended up 113.49 points, or 1.65%, at 7,007.72, its highest closing level since September 10.
** Heavyweight chipmakers Samsung Electronics
rose 4.98% and peer SK Hynix
gained 0.59%.
** South Korea's exports for the first 20 days of this month hit a record high on a surge in chip sales, customs data showed on the day.
** In the US, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
rose 2.8% on Friday.
** Of the total 914 traded issues on the KOSPI, 310 shares advanced, while 552 declined.

** "The chip sector was a rare gainer, with Samsung Electronics rising sharply on expectations of price hikes," said Seo Sang-young, an analyst at Mirae Asset Securities. "There are investor hopes around several AI-related conferences this week as well as US talks with Iran and China."
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 3.30%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 1.64% and down 1.56%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.86%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 0.29%.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 171.9 billion won ($124.38 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,381.0 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.33% higher than its previous close at 1,385.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.05 point to 102.24.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 2.0 basis points to 4.047%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 1 basis point to 4.450%.
